definition: the technical *capabilities* layer: compute, networking, storage, delivery (GitOps/CI/Kargo), secrets, identity-as-a-service, observability, the AI platform and the data platform. Business-agnostic — it would survive unchanged if the company stopped selling insurance.

the *applications, data and processes* that run the insurer: policy, claims, underwriting, billing, the digital workplace, ERP, ITSM, IAM governance, compliance. It *consumes* platform capabilities. (Provider ↔ consumer: Platform provides, the IS consumes.)
the RNCP39583 certification project: a real DORA third-party-ICT compliance product that *runs on and benefits from* the IS. Distinct from the IS itself (the IS is its organisational context).

(same letters, different things) — **IDP** = *Internal Developer Platform*, the paved-road self-service layer (Backstage, GitOps/ArgoCD, Kargo, the wrapper-chart golden path). **IdP** = *Identity Provider*, the SSO/OIDC service (Authentik). These docs mean **IDP** unless they say *Identity Provider*.

The *one* authoritative place a fact officially lives; if two systems disagree, the SoR wins. For access, the **ktayl-iam catalog** (`application → role → group`) is the SoR for *who may access what*.
The system that authenticates users and issues identity tokens. Here = **Authentik** (SSO for every app). *(Not the same as **IDP** = Internal Developer Platform.)*
Enforces an access decision at runtime but doesn't *own* it. Here = **Authentik** (checks the group at login).
**PDP** = Policy *Decision* Point (evaluates the rule); **PAP** = Policy *Administration* Point (where rules are authored). ktayl-iam is the PAP/decision source; Authentik enforces.
Role-Based Access Control — access via *roles* (groups), not per-user. Tools map the OIDC `groups` claim → a role.
Attribute-Based Access Control — access from *attributes* (country, line-of-business), layered on RBAC.
Identity Governance & Administration — the lifecycle of *who should have what* (request, approval, provision, recertify). The **ktayl-iam** product.
The identity lifecycle events IGA governs (onboard → role change → offboard).
Single Sign-On — one login (Authentik) for all apps.
OpenID Connect — the SSO protocol; carries identity + a **`groups` claim** the tools read for RBAC.
An ingress-level auth check for apps that can't speak OIDC — Authentik authorizes the request before it reaches the app.
A field inside the OIDC token (e.g. `email`, `groups`) the app trusts.
(least privilege) — A lower tier **cannot** perform a higher tier's action (Developer → Viewer, not Admin). A *read-vs-write* control.
No *one person* holds two **conflicting** duties — e.g. **request** AND **approve** their own access (maker ≠ checker). An *anti-fraud* control, distinct from least-privilege.
An emergency credential/path used only when normal SSO is down (e.g. Vaultwarden master login).
Git is the single source of truth for the desired cluster state; a controller continuously reconciles the cluster to match it.
the GitOps controller here: it reconciles one environment from Git and auto-syncs it.

promotes one immutable image across stages by *writing the Git change* (opening PRs) that ArgoCD then deploys. Division of labour: **CI builds & proves the artifact; Kargo promotes it; ArgoCD deploys it.**
(Kargo) — a *Warehouse* watches for new artifacts; a *Freight* is a promotable set (an image or a commit); a *Stage* (dev, prod) is an environment a Freight is promoted to.
the Helm golden path: a custom app is a thin chart depending on the shared `minicloud-app-deployment` library chart. One Helm render, one ArgoCD source.
the prod approval lives in Git: a PR touching a gated path (prod overlays, `services/*/helm`, `apps/`, `helm-values/`, `.claude/`) requires code-owner review before merge.
an always-on required CI check that scans every PR for unresolved git conflict markers.
the hybrid registry: **Harbor** holds dev/ephemeral images; **ghcr.io** holds the durable, immutable-SHA prod images.
supply-chain controls: keyless image signing, a software bill of materials attached to the image, and a CRITICAL-severity vulnerability scan gate.

(*mise en production*) — the moment a validated change reaches the prod environment. Here it is a human-approved, CODEOWNERS-gated promotion: Kargo opens the Git change, ArgoCD reconciles it. *Example:* a custom service auto-deploys to dev, then waits for a reviewed prod PR — see the [System Design case](/system-design).
the story-authoring workflow (intent → spec → stories → build → review), organised per product.
the artefact burden scales to the work: **A** small change · **B** feature/epic · **C** new product/major initiative · **E** emergency/hotfix.
L0 static · L1 unit · L2 integration (real DB/queue) · L3 contract · L4 e2e/smoke.
an adversarial test pass against the *live dev* service, mandatory before prod promotion (catches integration/deploy/runtime bugs that mocked tests cannot).
the lightweight Kubernetes distribution the cluster runs on (6 nodes).
the eBPF CNI (networking + NetworkPolicy + Hubble observability).
the distributed block storage providing network-attached PersistentVolumes.
the Postgres operator and the database standard: HA failover + PITR backups.
External Secrets Operator delivers secrets from HashiCorp Vault into pods; no secret material is ever committed to Git.
the identity provider: SSO/OIDC + MFA that every app trusts. Identity is the perimeter.
issues TLS certificates from the internal `minicloud-ca` ClusterIssuer.
the messaging backbone for event-driven, asynchronous workflows.
private mesh access (internal) and public ingress (for published apps).

(*service cloud managé*) — a capability I rent and someone else operates, instead of running it on my own hardware. The hybrid rule: self-host by default, use a managed service where it covers a risk better than I can. *Example:* Cloudflare R2 holds the off-site backup copy and Amazon SES sends outbound mail — the responsibilities I deliberately delegate (see the [System Design hybrid case](/system-design)).
the reliability *objective*, the *indicator* that measures it, and the `1 − SLO` allowance whose burn gates risky changes.
Recovery Time Objective (how fast service is restored) and Recovery Point Objective (how much data loss is tolerable) — proven by DR drills.
a deliberately induced failure, measured and written up in a postmortem — reliability as evidence.
Mean Time To Recovery: how long it takes to recover from an incident.
the EU Digital Operational Resilience Act (ICT risk, third-party-ICT, resilience testing).
risk-tiered obligations for AI systems; controls scale with the tier.
EU data-protection regulation governing personal-data handling.
the EU prudential framework for insurers (the regulatory spine of the IS).

(*rapprochement comptable*) — confirming that two records of the same money agree: here, that each premium billed this month is also posted to the general ledger, with any gap surfaced. The basis of an honest period close. *Example:* the `ktayl-core` finance close walks invoice → GL and flags mismatches — see the [System Design case](/system-design).
